articles.headline: Preece Expected to Remain at RFK Through Contract Term
articles.dek: Ryan Preece enters the offseason secure in his current seat following a productive campaign.
articles.body:
Silly season chatter has centered on multiple roster spots across the Cup Series garage as teams lock in their plans for the next year. Ryan Preece is signed through 2027 with RFK Racing, providing stability for the organization after a three-win season that yielded 959 points and a sixth-place finish in the standings.

Sources indicate that despite external speculation regarding various garage openings, Preece remains focused on his current commitments. The team management values the consistency shown through the 36-race schedule, particularly during victories like the one at Talladega.

Other operations continue evaluating personnel and equipment adjustments during the downtime. With the conclusion of the Homestead event, official announcements regarding technical alliances and remaining open positions are expected to surface across the industry in the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Buescher Salvages Ninth in Final Standings Following Charge
articles.dek: Chris Buescher advanced 31 positions during the Homestead finale to secure thirteenth in overall points.
articles.body:
The final race of the year at Homestead-Miami Speedway required patience and track position management across 200 laps. Chris Buescher executed both after qualifying thirty-fifth in the RFK Racing entry. Seven caution periods shaped the afternoon, allowing strategy to play a major role in the midfield.

Buescher capitalized on handling adjustments to march through the field. He led 19 laps during varying pit cycles before crossing the stripe in fourth place. That performance capped a season where the team collected 835 points, establishing a solid baseline for the upcoming winter break.

Further up the finishing order, Tyler Reddick pushed his #45 machine to second after starting thirty-first, leading 33 laps in the process. Austin Cindric also found speed from a seventh-place start, pacing 19 circuits and finishing fifth. These late-race charges highlighted the competitive balance across intermediate layouts as the 2026 campaign officially concluded.

articles.headline: Ty Gibbs Wins Homestead Finale as Chase Briscoe Claims Title
articles.dek: Ty Gibbs drove from nineteenth to win the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway while Chase Briscoe secured the championship.
articles.body:
Ty Gibbs captured the checkered flag in the season-ending Straight Talk Wireless 400 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, navigating 200 laps and seven cautions to take his fourth win of the year. Gibbs started nineteenth and sliced through the field, leading 66 laps on his way to the victory.

Tyler Reddick chased Gibbs across the finish line, coming home second after a charge from thirty-first on the grid that included 33 laps led. Chase Briscoe completed the podium in third, leading 26 laps to cement his championship run and cap off a six-win campaign. Chris Buescher earned the biggest mover honors of the afternoon, advancing 31 positions from thirty-fifth to finish fourth.

Behind the leaders, Austin Cindric placed fifth with 19 laps led, followed by Christopher Bell in sixth. Michael McDowell finished seventh, AJ Allmendinger eighth, Joey Logano ninth, and Denny Hamlin rounded out the top ten after starting twenty-fourth.

In the final season standings, Chase Briscoe holds the top spot with 1224 points and six wins. Ty Gibbs finishes second with 1122 points and four victories, while Denny Hamlin takes third with 1059 points and eight wins. Christopher Bell is fourth at 1050 points, and Tyler Reddick rounds out the top five with 1028 points.

The Cup Series now enters the offseason, giving teams time to prepare for the next championship chase.

articles.headline: Daytona Opener Statistics Reveal Pack Efficiency Trends
articles.dek: A detailed look at the numbers behind the 188-lap season opener at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.body:
The opening race of the sim-racing season at Daytona International Speedway brought 188 laps of intense pack racing, featuring seven caution periods that shaped the afternoon. Christopher Bell led the field for 78 laps on his way to victory, establishing early control of the race from the eighth starting position.

Moving through the field proved possible for disciplined drivers willing to bide their time. Ryan Blaney made the largest forward charge of the afternoon, climbing twenty positions from 28th on the starting grid to finish eighth. Ryan Preece advanced eighteen spots from 23rd to finish fifth, while Riley Herbst gained eighteen positions from 24th to sixth. Kyle Busch also worked his way forward, advancing fifteen spots from 22nd to seventh.

At the front, Ty Gibbs led 25 laps and finished second, followed by Erik Jones with 19 laps led in third position and Chase Briscoe leading 16 laps to take fourth. Todd Gilliland and Daniel Suárez rounded out the top ten without leading laps, starting ninth and twelfth respectively.

Attrition played a notable role in the final rundown. Carson Hocevar and William Byron exited the event due to accidents, while Denny Hamlin was sidelined by damage vehicle policy rules and Joey Logano suffered an engine failure. The race concluded with a margin of victory of 0.806 seconds.

Attention now shifts to EchoPark Speedway for the Autotrader 400, where the model lists Ty Gibbs at thirteen percent win probability and Christopher Bell at ten percent.

articles.headline: Christopher Bell Wins Daytona 500 to Open Sim Cup Season
articles.dek: Christopher Bell dominated the closing laps at Daytona International Speedway to capture his first career Daytona 500 victory.
articles.body:
Christopher Bell started eighth, led a race-high 78 laps, and held off a charging pack through a 0.806-second margin of victory to win the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season opener at Daytona International Speedway. The race featured 36 starters, seven cautions, and multiple attrition points that thinned the lead lap.

Ty Gibbs finished second after leading 25 laps, while Erik Jones claimed third after pacing the field for 19 circuits. Chase Briscoe finished fourth and Ryan Preece completed the top five after charging from his 23rd-starting position. Riley Herbst, Kyle Busch, and Ryan Blaney also made significant forward moves through the field during the 188-lap event.

Early race incidents shaped the running order, with Carson Hocevar and William Byron exiting due to accidents. Denny Hamlin dropped out under the damaged vehicle policy, and Joey Logano retired due to engine failure.

With the opening event complete, Christopher Bell leads the standings with 55 points and one win, followed by Ty Gibbs with 35 points and Erik Jones with 34 points.

The NASCAR Cup Series moves to its second round of the 36-race season next week.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

chase.headline: Finalizing the 2,500 Simulation Runs
chase.summary: Looking back across the full schedule, Chase Briscoe established ultimate dominance with 1,224 points. Ty Gibbs secured second position in the final tally with 1,122 points while Denny Hamlin completed the top three at 1,059 points.

race.headline: Breaking Down the Finale Performances
race.summary: Ty Gibbs delivered a massive performance by driving from nineteenth to win the season finale. Chase Briscoe capped off his title run with a third place finish after leading 26 laps, while Tyler Reddick drove from thirty-first to take second.

notes.ty gibbs: Charged forward from nineteenth on the grid to capture the final victory of the year.
notes.tyler reddick: Mounted a stellar recovery from thirty-first to secure the runner-up position.
notes.chase briscoe: Capped his championship campaign by pacing 26 circuits and placing third.

season.headline: Reflecting on a Complete 36 Race Campaign
season.summary: The books are officially closed on thirty six rounds of sim racing after a grueling calendar. Drivers like Ryan Preece left their mark by breaking long winless droughts late in the year, proving perseverance pays off over a full schedule.

notes.ryan preece: Snapped a 20-race winless drought with a dominant performance at Talladega.
notes.chris buescher: Showcased strong late-season pace by climbing 31 positions to finish fourth in a standout drive.
notes.ryan blaney: Charged from fifteenth to fifth and paced 28 laps during a stellar closing stretch.
